pr_body:
Calculating the autoscaling capacity can take considerable time and
has therefore been moved off transport threads. Also, we ensure that
only one thread calculates capacity and only compute one result if
multiple requests are pending, serving all pending requests in one go.
Finally, the capacity requests are now cancellable.

Closes #79104

Backport of #80499

issue_context.title: Autoscaling capacity calculation blocks a transport thread
issue_context.body:
**Elasticsearch version** (`bin/elasticsearch --version`): seen in 7.13.1 but `master` also affected

**Plugins installed**: [Cloud]

**JVM version** (`java -version`): Bundled

**OS version** (`uname -a` if on a Unix-like system): Cloud

**Description of the problem including expected versus actual behavior**:

In a 100-node cluster with ~23k shards we saw the get-autoscaling-capacity API taking 10-20 seconds to complete its calculations. However this API runs on `SAME`, so while the calculation was ongoing it blocked other network activity on the same worker.

review_comments: NIT: Looks like `org.elasticsearch.core.List.of(...)` produces unmodifiable list as well so above could be simplified.
I am not sure I follow how this could be used here. `List.of` expects individual elements, but here we have a collection of roles that need conversion to an unmodifiable list.
Should this be a static inner class?
Yeah, that would be nice. I prefer to keep this in sync with master though we can follow-up to fix this.
